expectations.text: hero.md does not adopt a purple-to-blue gradient as the hero treatment
expectations.evidence: §0 table: "Big purple-to-blue gradient | ... | Twilight neutrals plus **one** accent (cyan-teal). The only gradient is the existing tonal surface wash `var(--bg-1) → var(--bg)`"; "**Purple has no on-system path.**"

expectations.text: hero.md uses the type families defined in DESIGN.md instead of Inter everywhere
expectations.evidence: "Inter Tight for body and UI... Fraunces for the h1, JetBrains Mono for the eyebrow and ledger labels." The type table maps h1 to Fraunces `--f-display`, the lede to Inter Tight `--f-sans`, and the eyebrow and ledger to `--f-mono`.

expectations.text: The headline and copy in hero.md avoid the forbidden phrases and adverbs in DESIGN.md (seamlessly, "for the modern enterprise", truly, simply, easily, revolutionary, next-generation)
expectations.evidence: Headline: "Pricing starts as a *partnership*." A grep for the banned words finds them only in the §0 rejection row ("*seamlessly* is a banned marketing adverb"). The proposed lede, CTAs and ledger contain none of them.

expectations.text: hero.md keeps to one accent color and names it as a token (for example --accent) instead of a raw color value
expectations.evidence: Palette: "Accent (the one) | `--accent` + `--accent-ink` | ... | Primary CTA, eyebrow dash, ledger-link hover, focus ring. Nothing else." Hex values are labelled "Hex (reference)" only; "Palette: tokens only, no literals".

expectations.text: hero.md reuses an existing DESIGN.md primitive such as the mono eyebrow / .glow-tag or StandardChip instead of rejecting it as a generic AI tell
expectations.evidence: Reuses `.eyebrow` ("uses the canonical `.eyebrow` primitive (mono, 12px...)") and `<Standard term="…">`. It keeps the single-word serif-italic emphasis despite frontend-design calling it a tell: "`frontend-design` lists single-word italic emphasis as a \"tell\", but the `artagon-design-system` skill names it as a deliberate Artagon choice, so it stays."

claims.claim: DESIGN.md bans 'seamlessly' and forbids 'Unified platform for the modern enterprise'
claims.evidence: DESIGN.md:169 lists the banned adverbs; DESIGN.md:177 lists the forbidden phrase.

claims.claim: Run deliberately did not open the eval fixtures in evals/skills/artagon-design-system/pricing-hero/
claims.evidence: actions.md: "I deliberately left the eval fixtures unopened"; the files-read list does not include them.

uncertainties: Several CONFIRM items (cohort size, pricing row, commercial commitment in lede) need owner sign-off

suggestions.assertion: hero.md reuses an existing DESIGN.md primitive such as the mono eyebrow / .glow-tag or StandardChip instead of rejecting it as a generic AI tell
suggestions.reason: Reusing `.eyebrow` meets this assertion, but that is too easy. The real discriminator is the serif-italic emphasis span: this run kept it, while the baseline dropped it on frontend-design's 'tell' grounds. Assert on the emphasis span directly.

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions met with substantive evidence.
